items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I recorded for a singer named Eddy Howard and the group included Benny Morton on trombone, Edmond Hall clarinet, Bud Freeman, a popular white tenor man, the famous Charlie Christian on guitar, Billy Taylor, Sr., Yank Porter, and Eddie Gibbs on guitar.

ctx.x: I said I would explain why I thought Lew the barman was a great person. Barney was a real liberal boss and a communist. He gave us a special price for drinks and it was Lew who served us. Al Hall and myself were the heaviest drinkers in the band. In fact we were the only two in the group that drank. Other than Yank, who smoked cigars, we were the only two in the group who smoked cigarettes. The popular drink at the moment was rum and coca cola and Lew was very heavy-handed with us when we went into the bar for a…

The 4th of October, I recorded for a singer named Eddy Howard and the group included Benny Morton on trombone, Edmond Hall clarinet, Bud Freeman, a popular white tenor man, the famous Charlie Christian on guitar, Billy Taylor, Sr., Yank Porter, and Eddie Gibbs on guitar. The 9th of December was a date with Teddy Wilson's orchestra for an ex-Benny Goodman singer named Helen Ward with George James, a baritone sax player, and Eddie Gibbs added to Teddy's group.

In December 1940, Barney Josephson branched out and opened a Cafe Society Uptown on East 58th Street, and it was a real plushy joint. The Cafe Society Downtown was not a very large place, and there was only one small dressing room for musicians and entertainers. But at the Uptown, the whole building was occupied by the club and there was a big dressing room for the two bands, the Golden Gate Quartet and the Boogie Woogies. There were at least 4 other dressing rooms quite large and they were all on the third floor.
